name: Pluralist democracy
summary: Pluralist democracy is large-scale representative democracy in which power over public matters is spread among many relatively autonomous organizations, parties and interest groups that compete, bargain and check one another, with the state among them. Its defining thinker, Robert Dahl, describes it through the institutions of polyarchy (near-universal suffrage, free and fair elections, free expression, alternative sources of information and freedom to form autonomous organizations, above all opposition parties) and traces its argument to Madison, who held that the mischiefs of faction are best controlled by enlarging the republic and dividing power. The common good is understood as a thin balance among conflicting interests, not one goal shared by a homogeneous citizen body.
scope: Pluralist democracy as Robert Dahl set it out (Who Governs?, Polyarchy, Dilemmas of Pluralist Democracy, summarized in his 1984 lecture 'Polyarchy, Pluralism, and Scale') and as the International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences and Krouse's review of Dilemmas describe it, with Madison's Federalist Nos. 10 and 51, which Dahl and Krouse treat as its founding argument. It excludes the British pluralists' attack on state sovereignty (Laski, Figgis, Cole) and the later identity-group pluralism the IESS describes, which are other strands, and value pluralism as a moral philosophy.

notes: Later pass under rules 5 (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-10). The first pass rested mostly on Wikipedia and on general values (tolerance, diversity) applied to specific statements; those answers are nulled, each with its reviewHistory, and only positions the defining texts state are kept. Pluralist democracy is a theory of how power is distributed in large-scale democracy, so its defining texts are silent on most policy, social, ecological, technological and foreign questions. Its economics split: Madison makes protecting unequal property 'the first object of government', while Dahl's Dilemmas of Pluralist Democracy calls for greater economic equality and democratic, employee control of corporations; Dahl's own remedies are recorded where they answer a statement. Themes searched: government and elections (Dahl's institutions of polyarchy, the Federalist papers), economy (Dilemmas via Krouse and the Wilson Quarterly review), world (an open copy of Dahl's 'Can International Organizations Be Democratic? A Skeptic's View' was searched for and not found; Cambridge holds it behind a paywall), society and religion. Dahl's books on archive.org (Who Governs?, Polyarchy, Dilemmas, On Democracy) are lending-only and could not be read; the SAGE Encyclopedia of Governance entry 'Pluralist Democracy' is behind a paywall; core.ac.uk refused a scripted download (403). The SEP 'Democracy' entry covers interest group pluralism but never uses the name, so it is kept only for the reviewHistory.
